reviews.author: Ashley Kim
reviews.text:
I went to Potler on a Saturday night on a friend's recommendation, and it was absolutely crazy.

There was so much variety that I was wondering what to eat first, but a new employee who looked like Sandara Park recommended the whiskey bar’s signature ‘flatter’. Each and every menu item was presented in a witty, clear and witty manner (the plating was also a work of art).

It comes with camping fire-shaped marshmallow cream, roasted marshmallows (they toast them with a blowtorch, but they come from the U.S.), pretzels, beer cheese sauce & spicy pine nuts, baguettes, celery, olives, etc. You can also refill the freshly baked baguettes!

My favorite was to spread beer cheese sauce on a baguette, it was amazing!! It was so delicious that it made me scream. This is my first time trying beer cheese sauce. It's not greasy at all and it's shocking. It was sauce. The chef who made it is a sauce master! Highly recommended for Season 2 of Black and White Chef!

I kept trying to make sure that all the food was just the right amount of sweet and spicy that anyone could eat. It's really difficult to do this, but each menu item was delicious as if it were the main dish.

The Portler Highball, which even I, as an Alssian, was so delicious, drank three glasses of, was so delicious, and my friends drank white port wine, and they seemed satisfied and started to be kind.

Delicious and enjoyable food that feels like storytelling, like nature in the city, with a view of the forest when you look up. It was a perfect Saturday night for me.

I'm so excited to see what events will happen during Christmas!! ☃️ Christmas Gwangkeul Reservations!!!
(Dogs are also allowed)

The space is cozy and luxurious, as expected from a cafe located in the wealthiest neighborhood in Korea.

They were selling Yemeni coffee beans, which are rare in Korea, so I paid a high price to try them.

reviews.text:

While thinking about this, I was curious about the specialness of this space, so I ordered a regular Americano. (I already had a good drip in Seocho last month.)

I thought that the regular Americano had a very balanced taste. The acidity was moderate, the taste of stir-fried beans was moderate, and the savory flavor was just right. (But I never used it.) That being said, I thought that it was a bit of a disadvantage in that it didn't highlight some of its unique features, but at the same time, I also thought that the mildness of the drink that I could drink while comfortably talking with friends was an advantage. I'm curious about what the higher-class espresso is like, but I'll come back next time when my pocketbook allows.

I think the structural features of the cafe are also worth appreciating. The roasting and esso area is very bright with full-length windows, and the auditorium has small windows to create a soft glow. You can choose the seats according to the visitor's style, and the subtle contrast between light and dark provides comfort. reviews.author: ethan ghymn
reviews.text:
I woke up in the morning and on my way to buy gimbap from Gwanghwamun Daily Bunsik, I was curious about it after seeing it in Peony's review last time, so I decided to stop by Purut Fruit, whose location I had checked while walking around the neighborhood, and try a smoothie instead of my morning coffee.

It opens at 8 a.m., so you don't have to worry about whether it's open in the morning. I arrived in front of the store quickly, so it felt empty as if it was a holiday morning, but when I entered the store, there were two people, and the younger one got up from his seat to look at his laptop at a table inside the store.

The drink menu consists of 4 types of juice, carbonated ade, smoothie with yogurt, and latte with milk. I want to drink a smoothie, but after scanning the menu, I like bananas, so I like things with banana in them, but since I ate a banana in the morning, I wanted to try fresh berries, but I was torn between the raspberry yogurt smoothie, which seemed to be a new menu item, and the blueberry yogurt, so I ordered a large blueberry yogurt. Select by size.

It is said that fresh fruits are used for seasonal fruits that are easy to store, and frozen fruits are used for berries that are not easy to store.

You're making a blueberry smoothie, and I see waffles on the menu, so it seems like croffles are trending these days, but I'm not particularly attracted to them, so I haven't tried them yet. Instead, I'd like to ask for one of the simplest whipped cream waffles among the waffles I'm familiar with.

First, the blueberry smoothie came out, and although it didn't have as much volume as in the US, it was definitely a good size in Korea, which made me smile.

When I take a sip, I don't feel the sweetness of the syrup like in a typical smoothie, but the refreshing tartness of the yogurt and the subtle sweetness of the blueberries. It feels good for my body, so it's nice because it feels like I'm starting my morning with a healthy meal.

They said it would take about 5 minutes to make the waffle, but when I looked at the waffle that was prepared and served, it was the size of a regular waffle, and the whipped cream inside had a good volume and apple jam was spread on it. After taking a picture, I brought it to the car and tasted it, which was wrapped in a paper box. It was freshly baked, and the waffle was lightly crispy and soft, and the whipped cream was solid, so it did not fall apart easily, and the sweetness of the apple jam combined with the subtle softness of the whipped cream made it perfect. I don't usually eat waffles, but it's been a while since I tasted them. It made me smile, and I liked the slightly sweet scent of Western food in the car, so I thought about not going to buy kimbap.

Overall, I don't usually drink smoothies, but the store I saw in Peony's review was close to my house and seemed to serve food carefully prepared by an owner I like, so I stopped by. The blueberry smoothie had the refreshing tartness of yogurt and the subtle sweetness of blueberries without the sweetness of syrup, and the price was cheaper than common franchises. The whipped cream waffle I tasted without thinking about it was surprisingly good, so I opened the store early in the morning. It was a visit I would visit again if I wanted a refreshing Western breakfast every now and then.

reviews.text: I found this pub by chance and it was a really nice beer pub. It is located inside an alley in Cheongdam-dong, and its name is unique because it is a famous Belgian monastery beer called Grimbergen. It is said that the owner named the store that way because it was the first beer he imported and sold. There is a beer display case in the middle of the room, and a variety of famous beers, mainly Belgian beers, are displayed. They also offer a few draft beers such as Weizen and IPA, but they mainly sell Belgian bottled beer. There are several types of expensive monastery beer that are difficult to find in general stores. I think this is a must-visit place for beer enthusiasts. In addition to beer, you can also drink wine, champagne, whiskey, and cocktails. The beer tasted good, the owner was friendly, and it was nice to be able to enjoy the beer in a nice atmosphere.

reviews.text: When you first enter the bar, your eye is immediately drawn to the carefully selected boxes of whiskey bottles lining the stairs. Concrete walls and floors create a soothing atmosphere with grained bar table tops, wooden trim above the seats, warm lighting, great contemporary jazz music, and impeccably clean glasses. I've never seen such a wide variety of whiskeys and a lineup of all distilleries in one place. The atmosphere is friendly and comfortable. If you have any questions about the whiskey collection, the store, or jazz, just ask Ha. He will be happy to help. My experience here was truly the best. Be sure to visit once. 10 out of 10! Highly recommended.
